armor_kit.identity: the kit id (8 hex digits, a number, or 0x and 8 hex digits), or its game name in any case when nameUnique; a shared name raises AMBIGUOUS_ARMOR_KIT
armor_kit.scope: every player wearing this armor kit reads its pieces (stocky, slim and any-body pieces alike)
armor_kit.writes: the weight of the kit's armor piece in that slot, in every body that has one: one guarded 4-byte write per piece

armor_class.scope: every armor whose pieces have this weight, for every player this machine simulates or hits
armor_class.writes: one f32 entry of the class table (reviewed executable data)

armor_damage_curve.scope: every Helldiver hit on this machine
armor_damage_curve.writes: one f32: the damage of one curve point; the armor values (x) are never written

transaction.expect: the vanilla currentDefault, or the value this Runtime wrote there; anything else is a CONFLICT
transaction.syncNote: Not synced: every machine evaluates with its own kits, tables and curve.

executableData: The class tables and the damage curve sit in game.dll pages that are executable at run time. They are written as reviewed executable data (the user's decision of 2026-10-08): only their exact 4-byte entries, after the build, every pin and constant are proved. The page protection is never changed (docs/armor-stats.md, "Class tables: reviewed executable data").

damageCurve.interpolation: linear between neighbouring points; the top value above the top armor value, 1.0 below the lowest

formulas.armorValue: A = the mean of the class armor value over the kit's armor pieces in the rating slots (torso, legs, arms, shoulders; not the cape or the hips), then the kit passive's armor rows: (Set, else the mean) + the sum of Add, times the product of Multiply. Read on every hit.
formulas.damageMultiplier: curve(A). The attack's penetration does not enter it.
formulas.speedFactor: S = the mean of the class speed factor over every armor piece of the kit (cape and hips included), applied at the next armor apply. How the game consumes S is unproven.
formulas.staminaFactor: F = the mean of the class stamina factor over every armor piece of the kit, applied at the next armor apply. It scales stamina drain and regen alike, and the jump, dive, climb and slide costs.
formulas.displayFactors: The armory averages the speed and stamina factors over the rating slots only, so for some kits the gameplay factors differ slightly from the displayed ones.

display.staminaRegen: STAMINA REGEN = 100 x (2 - F) (the display factor)

methods.describe: {entity, avatar, slot, armor_bonus, stamina_factor, armor_kit, derived, effective_armor_value, overridden}, or nil, code, reason
methods.set: writes one or both members: {status, code, reason, armor_bonus, stamina_factor, writes, verified}
methods.restore: puts the game's own values back where a member still holds this Runtime's value

armor_bonus.effect: added to the armor value of every hit on this avatar; the sum is clamped to -1..3 when the bonus is not 0
armor_bonus.lasts: live; a status effect writes -1 on apply and 0 on removal

stamina_factor.effect: the armor's F: scales stamina drain and regen and the action costs
stamina_factor.lasts: live until the game next applies the armor (a respawn or an armor change); call set again then

player.expectedState: each member holds the game's own value (armor bonus 0 or -1; the stamina factor the worn kit gives) or the value this Runtime last wrote; anything else is UNEXPECTED_STATE

sessions.summary: ArmorStatProbe 0.2.0 ran in the r55 build. The log shows the stamina factor 0.5, the kit ensure and the damage curve ensure applied and held (the curve with no protection change). Only one hit was logged, so no damage comparison exists. Recorded, not promoted.

evidence.validation: scripts/validate_armor_stats_snapshot.py (all seven retained snapshots) and the packaged scenario proof-armor-stats
